At enlargement, the mem in this refrain abbreviation seems to have a patach, like the other lines (וְ״מַ). Confirm whether the patach is printed or missing.
Is the mark under the tsadi a qamats or a patach (בְּהִצַּדְקוֹ)? At this resolution it looks like a patach.
In this line the letter shows a closed chet shape (שֶׁחוּא), unlike the he in the other refrain lines. Is this a printed misprint to be kept as שֶׁחוּא, or broken type for he?
What are the exact letters of the small margin cue before הַתָּם? The candidate's קר״ס is not confirmed. The first letter could be qof or samekh.

Read literally, the glyphs look like קונריס. Is this the Hebrew 'סוגרים' (close the Ark) in a small face where samekh and gimel look like qof and nun, or a different word? It is still pending human confirmation.
What is the small cue before תִּשְׂגַּב? It could be ח״ or a double-yod mark.
The glyphs look like סמַוטעט or סחָוטעט. Confirm the exact Hebrew-script spelling of German 'stimmt', with its vowel points.
The word after the cue ויאתיו looks like four glyphs (חיין, which would be 'איין' = ein) rather than אַן. Which is printed? The pointing of the cue word ויאתיו is also unclear.
Is the word before אָבער spelled עס, עז, or עש? The last glyph is ambiguous.

In וִיקַבְּלוּ עֹל מַלְכוּתְךָ, no holam is visible on על. Is it pointed or bare?
